> experiment with DFFs which use the charge in the gate capacitance to store a bit
<https://www.crowdsupply.com/wafer-space/gf180mcu-run-3/updates/a-need-for-speed-tholins-own-standard-cell-library>
Would such DFF require a minimum clock rate ?
aka be dynamic only ?
Yes
@kris Something sounds off in the "An Extra Bit?" section of the SRAM post.  It says "why they didn’t provide a 1 KiB macro " ... well they did.
And the table even lists it ... They didn't provide an 8 KiB macro.
or the table is wrong but in the same article "KiB" ought to be the same unit.
@tnt thanks for flagging that, i'll go back and double check it 🤔
@kris is the area really the exact same for the two small Tim Edwards macros? the 0.5 and the 2 KiB?
ah i must've copied the wrong results, the 2KiB is correct but the 0.5KiB should be 45860.87µm² - thanks @thomasflummer and sorry for the mistake!

you're correct, i was talking about word depth of the macro but used the wrong units - it should read "why they didn't provide an 8 KiB macro". i've sent off some corrections to clarify it, and in other spots where it might be confusing. thanks for spotting that

We are talking about the fact that the foundry SRAMs didn't include a `sram1024x8` version, which Tim created for his library, right? But isn't that largest size exactly exactly 1 KiB (= 1024 Byte)? The image description even says so: "Render of Tim's 1 KiB SRAM Macro".

The "Capacity (KiB)" column in the table should probably say "Capacity (Kib)" (note the small b for bit) or divide the values by 8, which I would prefer.
i think i'm getting my b's and B's confused 😅 what's the correct way of interpreting the IP name? the one you gave for example
`sram1024x8` means 1024 lots of 8 bits, so 1024 bytes = 1KiB.  For bits a lower case b is used (inevitably this distinction between bits and bytes is confusing!)

Hey all, planning on picking up wafers at 13:00 local (4hr from now)
Bring your anticipation 😂
Leaving to get wafers now..

The wafer.space gf180mcuD Run 1 ATBS ADC (digital core only) chip (JKU2) is alive! 🥳 
We successfully brought the digital core of our (Adaptive) Threshold-Based Sampling ADC to work. For the analog front-end, we reused the PCB-level prototype from my Master's thesis. Right now, only the base functions are tested. Next, we will test the adaptive threshold functionality and proper UART communication. It was already quite late yesterday, and some measurement devices were not available. 🙃
Started a thread.
Started a thread.

Oh incredible! Hoping to hold some raw dies or otherwise get microscope shots soon. The earlier I can get a close-up of the "color" palette I taped out, the faster I can get some more "colorful" art onto my run 3 die.

Small update about the eFuse. I've tested two more chips with eFuse from the Run 1. All Wishbone and async eFuse blocks at 5V worked flawlesly. WB blocks also passed 5 million reads endurance test without a single failed bit. This makes 3 successfuly tested eFuse chips in total. Not much, but I assume this means that WB & async eFuse blocks are safe to use in 5V designs 🙂.  Now for the downside, current SPI efuse wrapper contains an error which might lead to hold violations and SPI interface not functioning properly in some cases. So **please do not use the current SPI eFuse IP**. I'm planing to release a revised SPI wrapper in a couple of weeks, together with the 3.3V compatible eFuse IP with a separate 5V supply for writing.

I am not sure how we're doing things this run. As we only got a partial on die things are a little different on sending a few die to everyone.
I will try to get some microscope shots sooner than later. 
I'll also pick one of yours off and try to get a video though my scope to try to give idea of real life look.
That would be good, thank you
This is not going to be an exact science anyways, so, any close-ups at all helps.
Anyone taping out with my SCL this run?
The 3.3V SCL?
We do. Also one of our Run 2 chips was based on your SCL.

Okay, because, I added more cells to the SCL after run 2. I need someone to upgrade to this new version of my SCL for their run 3 tapeout so we can verify the new cells in silicon. Of course, the risk is that you'd be including cells that are not silicon proven, even if the rest of the SCL works on our run 2 dies.
But, people have reported a 10% or higher fmax improvement with the new cells.

I'm not sure if I will actually tape out anything this run, but if I do then I'd like to have a clock gate.  I thought maybe I could just instantiate one from the foundry 7t library, but trying that fails in detailed placement.  Maybe I could patch it into the Avalon SCL?
Dynamic only DFF's sound super dangerous and super cool at the same time 🙂
Did you see the awesome images that @InfoSecDJ did of people's parts?
It would be good to understand why it fails in detailed placement. I can't think of an actual technical reason it shouldn't work?
I'm **very** supportive of this! I would love us to get to the position where designing and iterating on our own standard cells is considered easy and normal thing to do.
@baragonaru - Getting some of @Tholin's new / updated standard cells into your projects seems like a very good use of your silicon.
Ah, I think it's just the site name in the lef.  Changing that locally to match the 3v3 SCL site name has got it past that step

Does the current template for wafer.space include the latest version of your library? Is there already in the newest version/any future plan to add falling-edge flops with reset? (Motorola used to define things happening on the falling edge of the clock...)
There are falling-edge flops, but none with async reset. I think you’re better off avoiding async reset anyways.
You will have to manually update, I believe
I will update the template within the next few days
thanks for the answers, guess I need to review the resets and keep the template up-to-date!
